question: Should experimental Claw manifests be allowed to create and share globally named MCP declarations, and if so what brokered command and host-authorization boundary governs that capability?
rationale: This is a new core security and ownership contract, not a mechanical bug fix: choosing a command broker, resource namespace, or explicit host-approved sharing policy changes the product boundary and persisted lifecycle semantics.

options.title: Require brokered, host-authorized MCP resources
options.body: Allow the feature only after stdio commands use an approved broker/allowlist and shared declarations require explicit host authorization or namespace isolation.

options.title: Restrict the initial feature to isolated declarations
options.body: Permit only per-Claw scoped MCP declarations and defer global sharing until a separate approved resource-sharing design exists.

options.title: Pause the MCP slice pending the RFC
options.body: Keep this stacked PR unmerged until the Claws RFC establishes the core-versus-plugin and MCP-authority model.

recommendation.title: Require brokered, host-authorized MCP resources
recommendation.body: Allow the feature only after stdio commands use an approved broker/allowlist and shared declarations require explicit host authorization or namespace isolation.
